title: In a large notification system, how do you stop a bulk marketing blast from starving time-critical messages (OTP/security): isolate priorities on separate topics/pipelines with their own dedicated consumer groups, so the critical pipeline keeps low latency even when the marketing pipeline is saturated or paused?
shortTitle: In a large notification system, how do you stop a bulk marketing blast from starving time-critical messages
keyPoints: Physical isolation by priority: separate Kafka topics with dedicated consumer groups for critical and bulk messages.
A shared queue causes starvation because millions of marketing messages sit ahead of the next OTP in arrival order.
Dedicated consumer groups give independent offsets, independent lag, and independent scaling.
Provider capacity must also be isolated: a shared rate limit still starves the critical path at the final hop.
A single priority queue is weaker because it shares consumers, provider rate, and failure modes.
The bulk pipeline can be paused during incidents while the critical pipeline keeps delivering.
Classify each notification at the edge so marketing can never accidentally enter the critical topic.

s1_definition.oneliner: Isolate priorities onto separate topics and pipelines with their own dedicated consumer groups and provider capacity, so the critical OTP pipeline keeps low latency even when the marketing pipeline is saturated or paused.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Starvation problem** – If OTP and marketing share one queue, millions of marketing messages sit ahead of the next OTP, ballooning its latency from seconds to minutes.
- **Physical isolation** – Separate Kafka topics for critical (OTP, security) and bulk (marketing), each with its own consumer group and worker fleet.
- **Independent scaling** – The critical group's progress is unaffected by the bulk group's lag; you can pause bulk without touching critical.
- **Provider isolation** – Reserve provider rate for the critical path with separate token buckets or credentials so starvation cannot occur at the last hop.
- **Edge classification** – Route each notification to the correct topic at enqueue time so marketing never enters the critical pipeline.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India has two counters: a dedicated express counter for urgent OTP and security messages, and a separate bulk counter for marketing. The express counter has its own staff and its own phone line. Even when the bulk counter is overwhelmed or temporarily shut during an incident, the express counter keeps serving urgent messages instantly because it shares nothing with the bulk one.

sections.s6_takeaway:
At National Bank of India, OTP, security alerts, and marketing shared one Kafka topic and one consumer group. When a scheme campaign enqueued tens of millions of messages, Rajesh's OTP sat behind that backlog and its delivery latency went from seconds to minutes, meaning he could not log in. The root cause was that critical and bulk traffic shared the same queue, the same consumer threads, and the same provider rate budget.

Pankaj split the traffic into two physically isolated pipelines: a critical topic for OTP and security with a small, steady, always-on consumer group and reserved provider rate, and a bulk topic for marketing with a large, elastic consumer group and the remaining rate. Classification happened at the edge, so marketing could never enter the critical topic. After that, a million-message marketing blast had zero effect on OTP latency.

During one incident, the team paused the marketing pipeline entirely while OTP kept delivering in milliseconds, which would have been impossible with a shared queue. The provider rate was also isolated with separate token buckets so marketing volume could never consume the OTP rate budget at the last hop. The principle is that the only reliable way to guarantee the critical path under a bulk flood is to ensure it shares no resource with the flood.

Remember one sentence: Isolate priorities onto separate topics with dedicated consumer groups and reserved provider rate, so the critical OTP pipeline keeps low latency even when the marketing pipeline is saturated, paused, or experiencing failures.
